claims.evidence: The presence of stickers suggests active use in a child's environment; physical wear on joints or surfaces is not detailed.
The report describes an upper section with doors and a lower section with doors.
Photo 0 shows a small oval mirror on the center door.
The witness report does not mention wheels or casters at the base.

risks.risk: Internal shelves or hanging rails may be missing or broken.
risks.proof: A photo or video of the wardrobe with all doors open.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as an empty shell without internal fittings.

risks.risk: Structural instability or damaged back panel (common in particle board furniture).
risks.proof: A photo of the back panel and a video of the unit being shaken to test stability.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having a loose frame or damaged backing.

risks.risk: Drawer runners or door hinges may be seized or damaged.
risks.proof: A video showing all drawers sliding and doors opening/closing smoothly.

risks.risk: The 'tyres' (wheels) claimed by the seller may be broken or missing.
risks.proof: A clear shot of the base/feet of the wardrobe.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a stationary unit without wheels.

proof_requests: Video showing the interior of all compartments.
Video of drawers and doors being operated.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as a standard children's wardrobe. It can be priced at its worst-case functional state, accounting for the cosmetic stickers and unverified internal condition.
